raw.description: Unofficial static recompilation of Bayonetta 2 (Switch) for Windows. Builds the game on your PC from your own legally dumped copy. No game files, keys or SDK code included.
raw.readme_excerpt:
# B2recomp

*by [K0NL](https://github.com/K0NL)*

**B2recomp** (short for *Bayonetta 2 Recompiled*) is an unofficial static recompilation of *Bayonetta 2* (Nintendo
Switch) for Windows. It translates the Switch version's AArch64 program code to C **on your own PC**, from **your own**
legally dumped copy of the game, and runs it natively on Windows with a re-implemented system layer (threads, file
system, audio, input, and the NVN graphics API on Vulkan).

It is not an emulator (no CPU interpreter, no JIT) and it is **not a way to get the game**.

> **This repository contains no game code, no game assets, no Nintendo SDK code, no firmware, no system fonts and no
> encryption keys, and it does not tell you where to get any of them.** It cannot do anything without a copy of the
> game you dumped yourself from a console and a game you own. Everything derived from the game (the translated code,
> the compiled game DLL, icons, shaders, textures) is generated on your PC from your dump and must stay there. Please
> do not share it, and do not open issues asking for it.

## Status

Measured on the developer's PC (Windows 11, 16 threads, a Vulkan 1.3 GPU):

| What | Result |
|---|---|
| Title screen, attract sequence, new game | runs |
| Prologue (cutscenes, chapter card, first fights) | played through: 900 s, no crash, every system call the game makes handled |
| Chapter 1 with a controller (DualSense, Xbox, Switch Pro and other SDL3 pads) | played by hand past the first part |
| Standard test run (`scripts/bench.py`: tutorial and the first fight, scripted) | 59.5 fps at 60 and 119 fps at 120 (the display rate), 0 faults |
| Frame rate 120 (beta) | the test fight at 119 fps on a 238 Hz monitor, each frame shown for two refreshes; combos, hit-stop, Witch Time, slow motions and stick-motion moves (back-forward, double tap) keep their 60 fps timing |
| HDR (Windows HDR on) | the picture goes out as HDR10, as bright as Windows' *SDR content brightness*, at no measurable cost (tested on an NVIDIA card) |
| PlayStation / Xbox button pictures (with the prompt mod) | with Face buttons by printed letter they follow the printed letters, the action prompts in play included (tested with a DualSense) |
| Later chapters | being played and tested |
| Other PCs and GPUs | run by players on AMD Radeon cards (RX 560 to RX 9070 XT), on Windows 10 and on handheld PCs; fixes for their reports are in v0.2.1 to v0.2.6 and v0.3.4 |

Expect bugs. Builds are compared with a scripted test run (`python scripts/bench.py`, see [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md)).

## The game is never downloaded

There is no prebuilt game, no `game.dll`, no `game_native.exe` to download, and there never will be: the game is
translated and compiled **on your PC, from your files**. What you can download is this source code, either alone or as
the **builder package**: the same source plus the free tools the build needs, so you install nothing.

## What you need

- **Your own extracted copy of Bayonetta 2, version 1.2 (update v131072) applied** (the ExeFS and RomFS as plain files; see
  [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md#what-you-extract-from-your-own-console)). The build checks that it is exactly that version
  and explains a mismatch. Encrypted packages (`.nsp`, `.xci`, `.nca`, ...) are refused: this project decrypts nothing
  and reads no keys.
- Windows 10/11 x64 and a GPU with a Vulkan 1.3 driver. A Linux version is in testing (the Linux builder on the
  **Releases** page, with its own `START HERE.txt`).
- **AMD Radeon RX 400 / 500 cards (Polaris):** AMD's Windows driver for these cards lacks Vulkan features that
  B2recomp's renderer normally uses (dynamic vertex input and pipeline libraries), and it offers no mailbox vsync.
  B2recomp works around that on Windows: the game runs (confirmed on an RX 560), but its first runs build more shaders
  while you play, so expect short hitches until they are cached, and vsync waits for the screen (FIFO). This is the

raw.description: Take the ads, tracking and clutter out of your Fire TV over ADB, no root. Every step can be undone. Comes with its own open-source home screen.
raw.readme_excerpt:
Your TV should do what you paid for.
Ads, tracking and clutter out of your Fire TV. Your apps and HDMI inputs stay.

dumbtv.org · Get started · What it blocks · Devices · Get help

As seen in TechCrunch · TechRadar · Tom's Guide · Gizmodo · XDA · It's FOSS · and more than 100 others

--- ## The story I had a Fire TV Edition television that had become painful to use. Menus lagged, apps took ages to open, and the home screen was mostly ads. When I looked, it had 129 MB of free memory, and much of the rest went to apps that started on their own and to Amazon services that report what you watch. So I asked a coding agent to clean it up over ADB, and [posted what happened](https://x.com/DevMuzzammil/status/2111595814099591535). People asked for the scripts, so I put them here and [shared them](https://x.com/DevMuzzammil/status/2111912547318395338). Since then, owners of about twenty other TVs and sticks have run it and sent back what they found. dumbtv is that cleanup, made safe to run on someone else's TV. ## What it does On a Fire TV stick, Cube or Fire TV Edition television, from your computer, with no root: - **Removes the ads and tracking.** Disables Amazon's sponsored rows, ad services, screen fingerprinting (ACR), telemetry and experiments, and turns off ad tracking and usage reporting. - **Blocks what cannot be disabled.** A small open-source DNS filter on the TV stops Amazon's telemetry and automatic updates from reaching their servers. Everything else, including your streaming apps, works as before. - **Replaces the home screen** with [dumbtv home](launcher/README.md): your apps, your inputs and a clock. 54 KB, open source, no internet access, no permissions. - **Leaves your apps alone.** Nothing you watch is removed un

# Aerial **给国产电视的一块干净桌面。** 参照 Apple TV 做的 Android TV 桌面：没有广告，没有推荐流，只有你的 App、壁纸和航拍屏保。
适合小米、TCL 等国产电视，开机自动进入，待机也不会被清理。 **中文** · [English](README.en.md) ![Aerial 首页](site/img/home.jpg) | 电视自带的桌面 | 换上 Aerial 之后 | |:---:|:---:| | | |
## 功能

- **首页**：常用的一排 App 放在屏幕下方的玻璃底板上，往下是全部 App。小米「应用中心」「米家」这类藏起来的系统 App 也在。 - **整理**：长按 OK 键（或按菜单键）可以移动、放进文件夹、隐藏、卸载。固定到主屏幕的 HDMI 可以选接的是 Apple TV、PlayStation、Switch、Xbox、电脑等，换成对应的图标，也能在手机上起名字；文件夹也可以在手机上改名。 - **控制中心**：在第一排按上键到右上角打开，有信号源、网络、设置、音量、亮度和个性化。 - **屏保**：Apple TV 的 114 段航拍影片，电视支持时播 4K 或 4K 杜比视界，也可以换成照片、时钟或从手机添加的本地视频（[说明](docs/SCREENSAVER_VIDEOS.md)）。 - **壁纸**：必应每日精选、14 张内置壁纸、用手机扫码传的照片，或者航拍：停在主屏幕 10 秒后在磁贴后面播放，按任意键停在当前画面。 - **个性化**：单排或双排、时钟大小和位置、App 名称、焦点样式、按键声音，都能改。

Exploits · Detection · Lab · Writeup

--- Five independent RCE chains exploiting PHP's `session.upload_progress` and the Zend engine's OOM bailout. **14 years of vulnerable code** — PHP 5.4.0 (2012) through 8.5.11. Pre-auth. # UniXNU 🎉 **News:** The native Metal GPU driver is now fully working on the Xiaomi Pad 6S Pro (sheng). The render server composites the system UI through the Adreno 740, and listed processes get their own Metal devices. See the [Adreno 740 driver documentation](https://unixnu.com/drivers/native-adreno). An independent project to run iOS and macOS on non-Apple ARM64 hardware through UEFI. ## Documentation The documentation is at [unixnu.com](https://unixnu.com). It covers the boot chain, the build driver, device porting, driver development, the 4 KiB XNU page patches, boot arguments and per-device notes. - [Overview](https://unixnu.com/guide/overview) - [Build](https://unixnu.com/building) - [Boot the image](https://unixnu.com/guide/boot) - [Debugging and logs](https://unixnu.com/guide/debugging) - [Porting](https://unixnu.com/porting/) - [Drivers](https://unixnu.com/drivers/overview) - [XNU and 4 KiB pages](https://unixnu.com/xnu/four-k-page-tables) - [Devices](https://unixnu.com/devices/) ## Repositories | Repository | Contents | | --- | --- | | [UniXNU](https://github.com/UniXNU/UniXNU) | Build driver, UEFI boot manager, module submodules and patches | | [UniXNU-sheng](https://github.com/UniXNU/UniXNU-sheng) | Device repository for the Xiaomi Pad 6S Pro | | [uefi-sheng](https://github.com/UniXNU/uefi-sheng) | UEFI firmware port for the Xiaomi Pad 6S Pro | Drivers and kits are independent public repositories under the UniXNU organization, included as submodules. Clone with `--recurse-submodules`, or run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. Device repositories use the same layout as this repository. Their modules override modules with the same name, and their `package/` becomes a kit in the build tree. ## Contributing Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the repository scope, the development workflow, the commit format and the documentation rules. ## Private blobs Do not add Apple IPSW files, kernelcaches, disk images, trust caches, Data seeds or vendor firmware to this repository. Keep them in a local cache or external storage. ## License BSD-2-Clause-Patent. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

raw.readme_excerpt:
# Free My TV **A fast, ad-free home screen for Google TV, LG and Samsung TVs.** Trending picks from your own apps, the weather at a glance, and a look that follows the sunset.
Open source. Built with Claude Code. One button to undo. [**freemytv.io**](https://freemytv.io) · [Install](#install) · [LG TVs](#lg-tvs-webos) · [Samsung TVs](#samsung-tvs-tizen) · [Any TV](#any-tv) · [Make it yours](#make-it-yours)
## What you get - **No ads.** No sponsored rows, banners or autoplaying promos. Not one. - **Your apps, front and center.** The streaming apps you actually use, on a glass shelf. Pick them and their order right on the TV. - **Trending, not sponsored.** Three fresh picks every hour from what's trending this week and the latest releases, only from apps you already have. Movies and Shows get their own tabs. - **Weather and markets, one press away.** The hour-by-hour forecast, sunrise and sunset, and live crypto prices. - **Light by day, dark by night.** It follows your city's real sunset, the way your phone does. - **A screensaver to match.** Full-screen photos of the picks with a big glass clock. - **Your own photos** (Google TV and Android TV). Send them from your computer (up to 100): the screensaver shows them, and without picks one is the home screen's background each hour. - **Fast.** 60 fps, every frame in 16.6 ms, on the TV's own chip. The home screen uses 96 MB of memory instead of 242 MB (−60%).
Measured on a 98″ TCL Google TV running Android 14. - **Set up on the TV.** Language, your city, temperature, theme, the weather and prices cards, which coins, and the apps on the shelf, in Free My TV's own settings. - **Safe.** No root. Nothing is uninstalled. One button brings back the factory home screen. ## Install About ten minutes. You need a Google TV or Android TV (Android 8 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi. ### The easy way: an AI assistant 1. **On the TV**, turn on developer mode: Settings → System → About → press *Android TV OS build* 7 times. Then Settings → System → Developer options → turn on **USB debugging**. Write down the TV's IP address (Settings → Network & Internet). 2. **On your computer**, open an AI coding assistant ([Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), Codex or Antigravity) and say: > Install Free My TV (github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv) on my TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon. It downloads the code, installs the tools it needs, builds the app and puts it on your TV, and asks before anything important. Swap in your TV's IP and your city. 3. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*. That's when the TV asks *Allow USB debugging?* for Free My TV: tick *Always allow* and accept. ### The manual way 1. **On the TV**, do step 1 above. 2. **Tools:** a JDK (17+), the Android SDK command-line tools (build-tools 34, platform android-34) and adb. raw.description: Capture iPhone LiDAR and photos, reconstruct editable Three.js rooms, and explore them in a browser.
raw.readme_excerpt:
# 3D Model Anything

[![Watch the video: 3D Model Anything](docs/images/thumb-1.png)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JGQCcCzuS88)

Capture a room on an iPhone, then use its geometry and photographs to build an editable Three.js scene with an AI coding agent.

[Open the office viewer](https://wesbos.github.io/3d-model-anything/) · [App support](https://wesbos.github.io/3d-model-anything/support.html)

This repository includes the **3D Model Anything iPhone app**, a **Three.js viewer**, the **scan-to-threejs agent skill**, and **Wes’s detailed office demo**.

The app records the evidence. The skill guides an agent through measurement, modeling and matched-camera visual comparisons. This is an iterative reconstruction workflow, not a one-click scan-to-perfect-model converter. The current workflow focuses on rooms and interiors.

## Run the viewer

Use Node.js 22.12+ (or a newer supported release).

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:5188. Explore the office in dollhouse, walking, overhead, wireframe and knolling views. The playground is at `/play.html?room=office-v4&mode=fpv`.

```sh
npm run build
npm run preview
```

The demo includes the reconstructed office and selected textures. Original scans and photo collections are not distributed; Scan and Overlay are disabled for this example. Those modes remain available for your own rooms with reference assets.

## Capture your own space

See [the iPhone app](apps/house-capture/README.md) for building with Xcode, device requirements, scanning and sharing. Scanning needs a LiDAR-equipped iPhone or iPad. Non-LiDAR devices can import and review scans.

The app is source-available here; an App Store release is a separate distribution step. Do not assume an App Store download is available yet.

Export a room or session through the system share sheet and extract it into an ignored `data/captures-in/<room>/` directory. Exports keep the existing `house-capture/5` contract; changing the app name does not change the files.

## Use the skill

The skill lives at `.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/SKILL.md`. Open this repository in an agent that supports local skills and ask it to use **scan-to-threejs** with your extracted export. You can also copy that skill directory into your agent's skill directory; the companion viewer/runtime in this repo is still needed for its capture workflow.

Example request:

> Use scan-to-threejs to rebuild the room in data/captures-in/my-room. Inspect the measurements and photos, create an editable scene, and compare rendered views with the original photographs.

Start with [the format guide](.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/references/house-capture.md) and [project layout](.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/references/project-layout.md). Helpers need Python 3; photo comparisons need Pillow, and optional depth reconstruction needs NumPy, Open3D and Pillow. Capture scripts use the `agent-browser` CLI.

A new room goes in `demos/<id>/` and is registered in `demos/index.ts`. The office example retains its earlier reconstruction layers (`office-v2`, `office-latest`, `office-v4`) to preserve the final geometry.

## Privacy and licensing

Only the office example is distributed. No other rooms, connected-house layout, original scan bundles, or development Git history are included. Keep your captures private; inspect assets before publishing your own demo.

Reusable source code and the skill are MIT licensed. The supplied office images/textures have separate [asset terms](ASSETS-LICENSE.md). Third-party marks, artwork and depicted products are not licensed by the code license.

See [release status](docs/release-status.md) for validation and iPhone distribution steps.

# tv-home

**Make a slow, ad-filled Android TV fast and clean again.** Debloat it over Wi-Fi and give it a
tiny Apple TV-style home screen with rotating nature wallpapers. You can hand the whole thing to
Claude Code with one prompt, or do it by hand with the scripts here.

![Before: Google TV home with a sponsored hero. After: clean dock over a Lake Louise wallpaper](before-after.png)

On a 2 GB TCL Google TV this disabled 25 bloat apps and cut the home screen's memory use from
192 MB to 83 MB. Everything is reversible: packages are disabled, never uninstalled.

## Do it with Claude Code (easiest)

1. On the TV: Settings → System → About → press OK on **Build** 7 times → back → Developer options
   → turn on **USB debugging**. Keep the TV on, on the same Wi-Fi as your computer.
2. Clone this repo, open Claude Code inside it (so it can reuse the launcher and scripts), and paste:

   ```text
   My Android TV is slow and full of ads. Find it on my Wi-Fi, connect over ADB, and debloat it:
   disable the manufacturer's ads, telemetry and junk (reversibly, never uninstall), asking me first
   about apps and features I might use. Then build and install a fast, minimal Apple TV-style home
   screen with a dock of my favourite apps and rotating nature wallpapers. Back up before changing
   anything, check every step with screenshots from the TV, and give me a restore script.

   Heads-up from people who've done this: use the adb-shell Python package if macOS blocks adb; on
   Google TV also disable com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith or it hijacks the Home button; and
   test the Home button from inside an app.
   ```

3. Accept "Allow USB debugging?" on the TV when asked, then answer a few questions: which apps you
   use, which go in the dock, whether you want wallpapers.

The prompt is short on purpose; Claude works out the details. The gotchas below are there in case it gets stuck.

## Do it by hand (macOS)

```bash
./setup.sh                                                  # Python ADB client, JDK 17, Android SDK
tools/find-tv.sh                                            # finds the TV, saves its IP
tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --probe                # model, Android version
tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-google-tv-g07/debloat.txt     # or your own list, see examples/
launcher/build-and-install.sh                               # build + install the launcher
```

Undo everything with `tools/restore.sh <the same list>`.

## What's here

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md) | The prompt for Claude Code / any coding agent |
| [launcher/](launcher/) | The home screen. 4.7 MB including the wallpapers; plain Android, no network, no background services |
| [launcher/res/values/config.xml](launcher/res/values/config.xml) | Dock apps, hidden apps, Live TV app, grid columns |
| [tools/tv.py](tools/tv.py) | Pure-Python ADB client: shell, batch, screenshots, chunked APK push |
| [tools/find-tv.sh](tools/find-tv.sh) | Finds Android TVs on your Wi-Fi |
| [tools/type.sh](tools/type.sh) | Type into the TV's on-screen keyboard from your laptop (`tools/type.sh` alone prompts hidden, for passwords) |
| [tools/disable.sh](tools/disable.sh), [tools/restore.sh](tools/restore.sh) | Apply / undo a debloat list |
| [examples/](examples/) | Debloat lists per TV model |

## The launcher

- Clock, greeting and date top-left. Frosted pills top-right for **Inputs** (HDMI/AV/Live TV

- A dock of your favourite apps. The focused app's name appears above it over a glow coloured from
  its banner. Press Down for every other app in a grid.
- 12 nature photos crossfade every 10 minutes, with a scrim so text stays readable. Swap them in
  `launcher/assets/wallpapers/` (1920×1080 JPEGs, credits in `launcher/WALLPAPER-CREDITS.md`).
- Deterministic D-pad focus, remembers the last tile, picks up newly installed apps on return.
